issue.title: fix(export): markdown export drops the transcript snippet when a citation URL cannot be parsed

summary: formatCitation in app/frontend/src/lib/exportMarkdown.ts renders each citation in an exported conversation, and three of its fallback returns drift from the healthy shape (a '- ' list item whose range line is followed by an indented '> "<snippet>"' blockquote): the two YouTube fallbacks (unparseable video_url, or video_url with no v parameter) drop both the leading '- ' marker and the quoted-snippet blockquote, and the Dynamous empty-lesson_url fallback keeps the snippet but lacks the '- ' marker, so entries merge into the previous list item and MISSION-required transcript snippets are silently lost from the export. The fix aligns all three fallback returns with the healthy-path shape. Only that one production file changes, plus acceptance tests appended to the existing test file, whose every current case must keep passing.

AC-1.given: a citation of default/'youtube' source type with an arbitrary non-empty video_title, video_url 'not-a-url' (unparseable), start_seconds 10, end_seconds 20, and snippet 'Relevant text'
AC-1.then: the returned string contains '> "Relevant text"' on its own line, i.e. the quoted transcript snippet appears as a blockquote line

AC-2.given: the same citation as AC-1 (video_url 'not-a-url', snippet 'Relevant text', start_seconds 10, end_seconds 20)
AC-2.then: the returned string starts with '- ' and still contains the fallback marker and timestamp range verbatim as '(timestamp link unavailable) — 0:10–0:20' (em dash U+2014 between the marker and the range, en dash U+2013 inside the range); on the unchanged tree the fallback emits no '- ' prefix, so this assertion is the RED proof of the deferred repro

AC-3.given: a citation with source_type 'dynamous' and an empty lesson_url (''), an arbitrary non-empty video_title, a non-empty snippet, start_seconds 10, end_seconds 20
AC-3.then: the returned string starts with '- ', contains no '](' (no markdown link), and still contains its '> "<snippet>"' blockquote

invariants: Every existing test case in app/frontend/src/lib/exportMarkdown.test.ts keeps passing unchanged; the issue requires that 'every current case must keep passing'.
formatCitation still returns the empty string when snippet is empty, whitespace-only, or undefined (existing guard, pinned by the current 'should return empty string for empty snippet' test).

The exact console.warn message '[exportMarkdown] Skipping timestamp link — invalid video_url: "<video_url>"' is still emitted on both YouTube fallback triggers (unparseable video_url and video_url lacking a v parameter); it is pinned verbatim by an existing test.

Healthy paths are unchanged: a citation with a valid YouTube video_url still yields '- [<title>](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>&t=<start>s) — <range>' followed by an indented '> "<snippet>"' blockquote line, and a Dynamous citation with a valid lesson_url still yields '- [<title>](<lesson_url>) — <range>' with the same blockquote (pinned by existing tests, including the full-export test).

After the fix, every formatCitation return path for a non-empty snippet begins with '- ' and carries its own quoted-snippet blockquote on its own line, so formatSources' newline join keeps each citation a separate Markdown list item and the reported merging symptom cannot recur on any path.
formatTimestamp, the export header, and the filename slug behave exactly as before.
out_of_scope: Backend, database schema, and any dependency changes — no new or version-changed packages are introduced.
The valid-URL (YouTube with a v parameter) and valid-lesson_url (Dynamous) return paths of formatCitation, except insofar as they serve as the reference shape the fallbacks must match.
formatTimestamp, the export header, and the filename slug.
Any production file other than app/frontend/src/lib/exportMarkdown.ts; acceptance tests are added to the existing app/frontend/src/lib/exportMarkdown.test.ts, which is not otherwise restructured.

Deduplicating the twin console.warn-plus-return blocks inside formatCitation (investigation-flagged separate-issue material); a fix that preserves observable output and the pinned warning may leave the duplication in place.
risks: The YouTube fallback entries must gain the '- ' prefix and the snippet blockquote without becoming links: the existing test pins not.toContain('[Test Video Title](') and toContain('Test Video Title') for the unparseable-URL case, so the bare title text and the absence of any markdown link must survive.
The console.warn message is pinned verbatim by an existing test; rewording, reordering, or dropping the warning on either trigger path turns a currently green case red.

Snippets are interpolated raw into the blockquote with no escaping; snippets containing double quotes or newlines will surface verbatim on fallback entries exactly as they already do on healthy paths. Do not add snippet escaping in this PR — it would either diverge the fallback shape from the healthy shape or widen scope.

If the implementer deduplicates the twin warn/return blocks, observable return values and warning behavior must remain identical on all return paths; otherwise minimal duplication-preserving edits are the safer change.

RED-proof authoring: acceptance tests should assert with string matching (toContain/toMatch) against the returned string rather than boolean assertions, so a red failure prints the actual fallback line containing '(timestamp link unavailable) — 0:10–0:20' and the deferred symptom stays visible in the checkpoint output.
